OSMR.name: Osmolyn Receptor
OSMR.description: Reports the Osmolyn concentration in the water touching the cell. The receptor only works embedded in the membrane; copies left in the cytosol, secreted, or merely anchored give the cell no reading at all.
OSMR.designBasis: extracellular solute receptor, akin to a methyl-accepting chemotaxis protein tuned to a compatible solute

OSMP.name: Osmoprotectin Synthase
OSMP.description: Synthesises Osmoprotectin, which shields the cell from Osmolyn stress in proportion to how strongly the gene is expressed. Any copy the cell actually makes adds to that shield.
OSMP.effectParameters:
Stressor: osmotic
Effect: limit shrivel in rich water
Two hyperexpressed copies settle at 0.1% shrivel
Further copies do not remove that last 0.1%
OSMP.designBasis: compatible-solute protection, akin to ectoine and trehalose synthesis used against osmotic stress

AQUP.name: Aquaporin
AQUP.description: A gated water channel in the cell membrane. Any transmembrane expression opens it fully, and extra copies do not move more water. The open channel lets water cross far faster than passive leakage, and closing it slows an unwanted flux. Immediate response, no storage.
AQUP.effectParameters:
Stressor: osmotic
Effect: survive
Gate: open while any transmembrane copy is expressed
Throughput does not scale with extra copies
Fast water flux, no storage
Water flux itself is not simulated yet
AQUP.interactions: most useful with OSMR supplying the gating condition
AQUP.designBasis: aquaporin water channels and mechanosensitive release, akin to AqpZ, MscL, and MscS
